A1.attack: A stranger with money pays an already-paid bill a second time.
A1.stopper: A bill can be paid once. Only an open bill can be paid.

A2a.attack: Close the loan outside Adag, then re-borrow the same debt against a quarter of the bitcoin.
A2a.stopper: Morpho's own 86% line stops it before Adag is reached.

A2b.attack: Close the loan, then re-borrow the same debt against bitcoin worth 60%, which Morpho allows, and pay a bill.
A2b.stopper: Adag sees the pledge shrank since its last check, so the 40% check runs.

A3.attack: Borrow up to half the bitcoin's value and pay a new bill in the same signature.
A3.stopper: Adag sees new debt, so the 40% check runs.

A4.attack: Pay a bill from cash, then borrow up to 60% after Adag's step in the same batch. Next block, pay another bill.
A4.stopper: Allowed by design, caught on the next payment.

A5.attack: A supplier pays its own bill.
A5.stopper: The payer can never be the payee.

A6_1.attack: A stranger writes a bill payable in cirBTC.
A6_1.stopper: Bills are in USDC or EURC only.

A6_2.attack: A stranger writes a bill payable in WETH.
A6_2.stopper: Bills are in USDC or EURC only.

A6_3.attack: A stranger writes a bill payable in a made-up token.
A6_3.stopper: Bills are in USDC or EURC only.

A6_4.attack: A stranger writes a bill for zero.
A6_4.stopper: A bill must be for more than zero.

A6_5.attack: A stranger writes a bill with a 141-byte invoice reference.

A7a.attack: A stranger cancels a supplier's open bill.
A7a.stopper: Only the supplier who wrote a bill can cancel it.

A7b.attack: The supplier cancels a bill after it was paid.
A7b.stopper: Only an open bill can be cancelled.

A8.attack: Pay a bill without approving Adag to move the USDC.
A8.stopper: The token refuses, and the whole batch undoes itself.

A9a.attack: Bitcoin drops 25%. Pay a new bill from cash, with no new borrowing.
A9a.stopper: Allowed on purpose: no new debt, so nothing to check. A price drop never blocks a cash payment.

A9b.attack: Bitcoin drops 25%. Borrow one cent more and pay the same bill.
A9b.stopper: New debt, so the 40% check runs.

E1.attack: Record the loan with enrol and pay a bill from cash in the same batch.
E1.stopper: A payer who enrolled in this block is refused, so a loan cannot be recorded and spent at once.

E2.attack: Borrow up to 60%, record that debt with enrol, and pay a bill, all in one batch.
E2.stopper: The same-block refusal: new debt cannot be enrolled and spent at once.

E3.attack: A stranger calls enrol, hoping to overwrite the demo payer's recorded loan, then the payer pays.
E3.stopper: enrol takes no arguments and only ever writes the caller's own record.

E4.attack: Enrol in one block; in the next, close the loan outside Adag, re-borrow it against bitcoin worth 60%, and pay.
E4.stopper: The pledge fell below the enrolled one, so the 40% check runs.

E5.attack: Borrow up to 60% outside Adag and enrol it; in the next block, pay a bill from cash.
E5.stopper: Allowed by design: enrol accepts the loan as it stands, and only the payer's own position carries the risk.

G6.attack: Call protect three times at the same price: twice in one block, once in the next.
G6.stopper: Each protect repays only what brings the loan back to the target, so a repeat finds nothing to do.

G1.attack: Pull more than the payer approved: the loan needs more than the 0.10 USDC approval, and protect runs twice.
G1.stopper: The approval is the lifetime ceiling, and protect caps at it.

G2a.attack: Protect the payer's loan through the other real USDC/cirBTC market on Morpho.
G2a.stopper: AdagGuard accepts only its two fixed market ids, checked against Morpho.

G2b.attack: Set a rule and call protect with a market id one hex digit away from Adag's.
G2b.stopper: A near miss is a different id, and it is refused.

G2c.attack: Protect the payer in the EURC market, where they have no loan and no rule.
G2c.stopper: Each market repays only its own loan, and only for a real, triggered rule.

G3.attack: A stranger calls protect while the loan sits under the payer's 50% trigger.
G3.stopper: Protect acts only at or above the trigger; otherwise nothing moves and nothing is emitted.

G4.attack: The payer's rule expires 60 seconds after it is set; a stranger calls protect at that second.

G5a.attack: A stranger clears the payer's rule.
G5a.stopper: Rules are keyed by the sender; nobody can name another wallet.

G5b.attack: A stranger sets a rule (80% / 1%) hoping it lands on the payer.
G5b.stopper: setRule writes only the sender's own rule.

G7.attack: The payer's wallet holds only 0.05 USDC when the loan needs more.
G7.stopper: Protect never pulls more than the wallet holds, and does not revert.

G8.attack: Bitcoin crashes to zero. Protect with a 2 USDC approval against the whole loan.
G8.stopper: The repay is capped at the debt rounded down, so Morpho's share maths cannot underflow.

G9a.attack: Bitcoin crashes to zero. Protect a payer who approved 1 USDC but has no rule.
G9a.stopper: No rule, no action, even at a zero price.

G9b.attack: Protect a wallet with no loan and no rule.

G10.attack: Call the admin functions a drain would need: transferOwnership, withdraw, rescue, pause and upgradeToAndCall.
G10.stopper: No owner, pause, rescue or upgrade exists; only setRule, clearRule and protect change state.

terms.title: The plain terms.
terms.lead: Short, because the contract does the talking. By using this website you accept the terms below.
terms.englishApplies: This is a translation for convenience. The English version of these terms is the one that applies.

whatAdagIs.title: What Adag is
whatAdagIs.body: Adag is a website that talks to one smart contract, AdagBills, on Arc mainnet. The contract is immutable: it has no owner and no admin key, and no one, including the people who built it, can pause it, upgrade it or change its rules. The website is only an interface to it.

youSign.title: You sign everything
youSign.body: Every payment, loan and cancellation is a transaction you review and sign in your own wallet. Adag never holds your money, never holds your keys, and cannot move anything without your signature. The contract passes the exact bill amount from the payer to the supplier within the same transaction and keeps nothing.

liquidation.title: Borrowing can end in liquidation
liquidation.body: Paying from bitcoin pledges your cirBTC on Morpho and borrows the bill amount against it. If bitcoin's price falls far enough, Morpho can liquidate the loan and sell part of your pledge. Adag refuses a payment that would leave the loan above 40% of your bitcoin's value, but it checks this only at the moment you pay. After that, interest and price keep moving, Adag does not watch the loan, and Morpho can liquidate once the loan reaches 86%. Watching and repaying the loan is up to you.

tokens.title: Tokens carry their issuers' risks
tokens.body: USDC, EURC and cirBTC are issued by third parties who can freeze addresses, pause transfers or change how their tokens behave. If they do, a payment can fail or funds can become stuck. Adag cannot override any of that.

noAudit.title: No audit beyond our own review
noAudit.body: The contract has not had a paid third-party audit. What exists is published: a threat model, a self-review with an attack suite simulated against the deployed contract on live mainnet state, and static analysis. The source of every contract is verified on the Arc explorer: <contracts></contracts>.

notAdvice.title: Not advice, not affiliated
notAdvice.body: Nothing on this site is financial, legal or tax advice. Adag is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or operated by Circle, Arc or Morpho.

ownRisk.title: Use at your own risk
ownRisk.body: Adag is provided as it is, with no warranty of any kind. You use it at your own risk, and you are responsible for checking every bill, every address and every transaction before you sign.

break.a4Fail: Did not behave as documented: first {first}; next {next}; bill {status}.
break.a5Pass: Refused. A supplier cannot pay its own bill: no money would change hands, so nothing would prove it was paid.
break.a61Pass: Refused. Bills are paid in USDC or EURC; cirBTC is the collateral, never the currency.
break.a62Pass: Refused. WETH is not one of the two currencies Adag accepts.
break.a63Pass: Refused. An address that is not USDC or EURC can never be a bill's currency.
break.a64Pass: Refused. A bill for zero is not a bill.
break.a65Pass: Refused. The reference is 141 bytes and the limit is 140, counted in bytes, not characters.
break.a7aPass: Refused. Only the supplier who wrote a bill can cancel it; the bill stays open and payable.
break.a7bPass: Refused. {label} is paid, and a paid bill can never be cancelled.
break.a8Pass: Refused. The USDC token would not move money Adag was never approved to move, so the whole batch undid itself and the bill stays open.
break.a9aPass: Paid, as promised. After the simulated drop the loan sits at {ltv}, but this payment adds no debt, so there is nothing to check.
break.a9bPass: Refused by Adag: one more cent is new debt, so it checked, and {over}.
break.e1Pass: Refused. A payer who enrolled in this very block cannot pay in it, so the whole batch undid itself, the enrol included.
break.e1Fail: Not refused as expected: {out}; bill {status}; enrol block {block}.
break.e2Pass: Refused. Borrowing {amount}, enrolling it and paying in one batch hits the same-block refusal; Adag's record of the loan is unchanged.
break.e3Pass: Held. The stranger's enrol went through but wrote only the stranger's own record; the demo payer's recorded loan did not change, and its payment went through.
break.e3Fail: Did not behave as documented: stranger enrol {a}; demo record {b} before, {c} after; demo payment {d}.
break.e4Pass: Refused by Adag: the pledge fell below the enrolled one, so it checked, and {over}.
